request.state: The task is to add compiler support for literal Money(amount,currency) model and parameter defaults while retaining explicit refusal for dynamic cases. Verified owner facts: an existing private Rust value crate exports exact decimal parsing, Money construction, and canonical scalar wire encoding; it applies pinned currency scales, one half-even rounding step and int64 minor bounds. Public JavaScript semantics match that owner. The monorepo native bindings use a Cargo path dependency on it already, without a compiler cycle. Its big-integer/formatting/serde dependencies are available locally. There is no stable external native API; catalog signatures cannot perform this fold. Evaluate each candidate against exact default behavior, avoiding duplicate semantics, maintaining ownership over time, implementation size, and the compiler remaining a standalone executable. Pick the smallest justified complete dependency boundary, with any uncertainty retained.

money_default_boundary.instructions: Choose using equal stated outcomes; weigh coupling against added API or host requirements and retain uncertainty.

criteria.direct_owner: Compiler directly consumes existing private Rust constructor/parser/codec exports through a Cargo path dependency, with a thin exact-literal adapter. Small complete reuse and standalone execution; acknowledges coupling to private paths/types and existing native crates.
criteria.owner_facade: Values gains a narrow supported constant-Money-folding entrypoint, backed by its existing parser/constructor/codec; compiler depends on that entrypoint through Cargo. Encapsulates representations but introduces an additional maintained API and owner changes with the same dependency graph.
criteria.public_js_process: Compiler launches installed public JavaScript Values to construct/encode defaults. Public semantics remain authoritative; an extra runtime/package and process protocol become required at compile time, increasing operational requirements while avoiding Rust private API coupling.
